name: neural plate
definition: Portion of tissue that is the earliest recognizable dorsal ectodermal primordium of the central nervous system present near the end of gastrulation before infolding to form the neural keel; consists of a thickened pseudostratified epithelium.

spatial.dv: dorsal surface of the embryo, over the notochord and paraxial mesoderm
spatial.landmarks: Dorsal midline from the anterior neural plate (future forebrain, near the animal pole) to the tail bud. Widest anteriorly.

shape.notes: Thick dorsal ectodermal sheet draped on the yolk sphere from 8 to 10 hpf. Model it as a spherical-cap strip. Width is about 300 um anteriorly and tapers to about 100 um posteriorly. Thickness is 3 to 6 cells anteriorly and 1 cell posteriorly.

sizes.source: estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length); embryo diameter about 0.8 mm at 5-9 somites, https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg_stgs.html

events.event: Presumptive neural plate specified in the dorsal ectoderm (ZFA presumptive neural plate starts at sphere).
Neural plate recognizable as a thickened dorsal ectoderm (ZFIN start, 75%-epiboly).
Convergence toward the dorsal midline starts; the plate folds into the neural keel (Araya et al. 2016 Dev Dyn 245:197-208 https://anatomypubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/dvdy.24304).
Plate no longer present as a separate structure (ZFIN end, 5-9 somites).

name: neural keel
definition: An intermediate stage (between the neural plate and neural rod) during the early segmentation period in the morphogenesis of the central nervous system primordium; the keel is roughly triangular shaped in cross section.

spatial.dv: dorsal midline, above the notochord
spatial.landmarks: Runs from the anterior head (optic primordium bulges laterally from the anterior keel) to the tail bud.

shape.notes: Solid rod with a triangular cross-section (apex ventral). Extrude a triangle of width about 80 um and height about 60 um along the dorsal midline spline. Anterior head end swells to about 150 um.

sizes.source: estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length)
estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length); embryo length 0.8 mm at 5-9 somites https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg_stgs.html

events.event: Neural keel forms by convergence of the neural plate (ZFIN start, bud).
Brain primordium thickened into the keel; optic primordium first distinguishable in side view (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg_stgs.html).
Keel rounds into the neural rod; three pronounced anterior thickenings visible (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg_stgs.html).
Keel stage over (ZFIN end, 10-13 somites).

name: neural rod
definition: An intermediate stage in the development of the central nervous system present during the segmentation period; the neural rod is roughly cylindrical in shape, forms from the neural keel, and is not yet hollowed out into the neural tube.

spatial.dv: dorsal midline, above the notochord
spatial.landmarks: Head end shows the ten neuromere swellings; trunk portion lies above each somite pair.

shape.notes: Solid cylinder of about 60 um diameter along the dorsal spline, without a lumen. Head end widens into a series of bulges (neuromeres).

sizes.source: estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length)
estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length); embryo length 0.9 mm at 14-19 somites https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg_stgs.html

events.event: Neural rod forms from the keel (ZFIN start, 5-9 somites).
About ten neuromeres visible along the rod; rhombomeres r2 to r6 visible dorsolaterally (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg_stgs.html).
Neural tube closure; brain morphogenesis begins (Lowery & Sive 2005 Development 132:2057-2067 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15788456/).
Rod hollows into the neural tube (ZFIN end, 14-19 somites).

name: neural tube
definition: Portion of tissue that is the cavity-containing primordium of the central nervous system, developing from the neural rod in the late segmentation period.

spatial.dv: dorsal midline, above the notochord
spatial.landmarks: The whole central nervous system from the telencephalon to the tail tip. Brain ventricles inflate along its anterior third.

shape.notes: Hollow tube: outer diameter about 60 to 70 um in the trunk, lumen (neurocoel) about 5 to 10 um. Anterior third swells into the three primary brain vesicles.

sizes.source: estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length)
estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length); embryo length 1.4 mm at 20-25 somites https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg_stgs.html
estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length); embryo length 1.9 mm https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/phar_stgs.html

events.event: Neural tube stage begins (ZFIN start, 10-13 somites).
Brain ventricle inflation begins (Gutzman & Sive 2012 J Vis Exp (ventricle inflation begins about 18 hpf) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23128341/).
Hollowing of the rod into the tube nearly complete; ventricles present along the brain (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg_stgs.html).
Cerebrospinal fluid starts to fill the ventricles (Lowery & Sive 2005 Development 132:2057-2067 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15788456/).
ZFIN end (prim-5); the model should switch to brain plus spinal cord terms from 24 hpf.

sources: Gutzman & Sive 2012 J Vis Exp (ventricle inflation begins about 18 hpf) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23128341/

name: brain
definition: Cavitated compound organ which is comprised of gray and white matter and surrounds the cerebral ventricular system.

spatial.dv: dorsal head, above the pharynx and notochord tip
spatial.landmarks: From the olfactory bulbs (anterior) to the obex where the medulla becomes spinal cord (about the level of the first somite / occipital region).

shape.notes: Union of child lobes. Larva: five lobes in a row (telencephalon, diencephalon, midbrain, cerebellum, medulla). Adult: same lobes. Add paired olfactory bulbs, paired everted telencephalic hemispheres, paired large tectal lobes, a single corpus cerebelli, and a medulla that tapers into the cord.

sizes.source: estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length); head occupies about 0.3 of the 1.9 mm embryo https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/phar_stgs.html
estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length)

about 400 x 800 x 250 um (W x L x H) at 5 dpf, about 100,000 neurons; State of Brain Emulation Report 2025 (secondary source) https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.15745; brain volume 5.49e7 um3 at 5.5 dpf, Hildebrand et al. 2017 Nature 545:345-349 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5594570/

Z-Brain reference stack bounding box, voxels 0.8 x 0.8 x 2 um (Randlett et al. 2015 Nat Methods 12:1039-1046 (Z-Brain, 6 dpf) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4710481/); stack extent about 500 x 1100 x 280 um (unverified, includes olfactory epithelium and anterior spinal cord)

length 4.5 mm, thickness 0.4 to 2 mm (State of Brain Emulation Report 2025 (secondary source) https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.15745 citing Wullimann, Rupp & Reichert 1996 Neuroanatomy of the Zebrafish Brain (Birkhauser)); width 2.5 mm is an estimate; AZBA regions span 0.000026 to 0.53 mm3 (Kenney et al. 2021 eLife 10:e69988 (AZBA, adult) https://elifesciences.org/articles/69988)

events.event: Brain term starts (ZFIN, 10-13 somites); four subdivisions visible by 16 hpf (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg_stgs.html).
About ten neuromeres: three large anterior ones and seven rhombomeres (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg.html).
Brain sculptured into five lobes (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/phar.html).
Larval brain about 800 um long; layered cerebellum and tectum present (Bae et al. 2009 Dev Biol 330:406-426 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19371731/).
Adult brain about 4.5 mm long (State of Brain Emulation Report 2025 (secondary source) https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.15745).

definition: The most anterior region the brain including both the telencephalon and diencephalon.

spatial.dv: anterior brain, dorsal to the mouth and pituitary
spatial.landmarks: Anterior to the midbrain; the eyes attach to it through the optic stalks.

shape.notes: Group node. Render as the union of telencephalon and diencephalon.

name: telencephalon
definition: The anterior and dorsal forebrain neuromere. In ray-finned fishes and most pronounced in teleosts the roof plate of the embryonic telencephalon extends laterally with the effect that the paired alar plates forming the hemispheric walls roll out lateroventrally in a process called eversion.

spatial.dv: most anterior and dorsal brain lobe, above the olfactory pits
spatial.landmarks: Anterior to the diencephalon; olfactory bulbs at its anterior tip; sits between the two eyes in the larva.

shape.notes: Larva: single ellipsoid with a shallow dorsal midline groove. Adult: two everted hemispheres, model as two side-by-side ellipsoids (each about 1.2 x 0.7 x 0.9 mm) fused ventrally.

Eversion of the telencephalic roof starts; hemispheres become visible (ZFA definition; timing unverified).
Adult everted pallium with dorsal, medial, lateral and central zones (Wullimann, Rupp & Reichert 1996 Neuroanatomy of the Zebrafish Brain (Birkhauser)).

name: olfactory bulb
definition: Brain structure which is the paired anteriormost part of the telencephalon and are connected to the telencephalon by two tracts carrying secondary olfactory fibers. From Neuroanatomy of the Zebrafish Brain.

spatial.dv: anterior tip of the telencephalon, at the level of the olfactory pits
spatial.landmarks: Directly posterior to each olfactory pit; connected to the telencephalon by short olfactory tracts in the adult.

shape.notes: Two small spheres at the anterior face of the telencephalon. In the adult they are distinct bulbs about 0.6 mm across on short stalks.

name: diencephalon
definition: The more posterior and ventral of two forebrain neuromeres, the other being the telencephalon; major derivatives are the eye cups, the brain pretectal region, the thalamus, hypothalamus, and epithalamus (including the habenula and epiphysis).

spatial.dv: ventral and posterior forebrain, between the eyes; hypothalamus forms its floor
spatial.landmarks: Posterior to the telencephalon, anterior to the midbrain; eyes attach here via the optic stalks; epiphysis on its roof, pituitary under its floor.

shape.notes: Ellipsoid wedge between telencephalon and midbrain; taller than wide in the larva. Contains the third ventricle.

name: hypothalamus
definition: Multi-tissue structure which is the largest portion of diencephalon and is ventrally located. The hypothalamus arises near the end of the segmentation period and the embryonic hypothalamic region gives rise to the neurohypophysis and other diencephalic nuclei.

spatial.dv: ventral-most forebrain, floor of the diencephalon, above the pituitary
spatial.landmarks: Ventral bulge of the diencephalon; the pituitary hangs from its floor; in the adult the inferior lobes bulge ventrolaterally.

shape.notes: Ventral ellipsoid under the diencephalon. Adult: add two lateral inferior lobes (each about 0.6 mm) so the ventral view shows a trilobed floor.

spatial.dv: ventral to the hypothalamus, dorsal to the roof of the mouth
spatial.landmarks: Midline, directly under the diencephalic floor, between and slightly behind the eyes. In the adult it sits in a shallow fossa of the skull base.

shape.notes: Small flattened ellipsoid pressed against the hypothalamic floor. Adult: oval about 0.5 x 0.35 x 0.3 mm (estimate).

name: epiphysis
definition: A circumscribed swelling, includes the pineal primordium that appears late in the segmentation period in the dorsal midline of the diencephalon. It is located directly rostral to the posterior commissure and dorsal to the habenular commissure.

spatial.landmarks: Dorsal roof of the diencephalon, rostral to the posterior commissure, between the eyes in dorsal view.

shape.notes: Small sphere on the dorsal brain surface. Adult: end vesicle about 0.3 mm on a thin stalk (ZFA epiphyseal stalk from 45 dpf).

name: habenula

spatial.landmarks: Two nuclei flanking the third ventricle under the pineal; the left dorsal habenula is larger with more neuropil.

shape.notes: Two ellipsoids either side of the midline; scale the left one about 1.2x. Internal structure; visible only in cut-away or transparent brain mode.

name: midbrain
definition: The brain region between the forebrain anteriorly and the hindbrain posteriorly, including the tectum dorsally and the midbrain tegmentum ventrally.

spatial.landmarks: Posterior to the diencephalon, anterior to the midbrain-hindbrain boundary constriction; largest dorsal lobe in the larva.

shape.notes: Ellipsoid with a dorsal midline groove separating the two tectal lobes; ventral half is the tegmentum. Contains the tectal ventricle.

name: optic tectum
definition: Multi-tissue structure that is the dorsal part of the midbrain and develops from the alar plate and is the most complex layered structure in the zebrafish brain.

spatial.dv: dorsal midbrain, directly under the skull roof
spatial.landmarks: Two dorsal lobes behind the eyes; the largest visible brain structure in a dorsal view of larva and adult.

shape.notes: Two dorsolateral ellipsoids (one per lobe) meeting at the midline. Larva: each lobe about 300 x 150 x 120 um at 5 dpf. Adult: each lobe about 1.6 x 1.0 x 0.9 mm (estimate).

name: hindbrain

shape.notes: Tapered tube widest anteriorly; dorsal cerebellum bump at its front, thin roof plate over the fourth ventricle. Embryo: segment the tube into 7 to 8 rhombomere bulges.

name: cerebellum
definition: Brain structure derived from the anterior hindbrain, and perhaps including posterior midbrain. The cerebellum plays a role in somatic motor function, the control of muscle tone, and balance.

spatial.dv: dorsal anterior hindbrain, directly behind the tectum
spatial.landmarks: Dorsal plate behind the midbrain-hindbrain constriction; in the adult the corpus cerebelli is a single dorsal lobe with the valvula tucked under the tectum.

shape.notes: Larva: transverse plate (wide, short, thin). Adult: single rounded lobe (corpus cerebelli) about 1.0 x 1.2 x 0.8 mm plus lateral eminentiae granulares; valvula hidden under the tectum.

name: lateral line system
definition: A sensory system on the surface of the fish, consisting of small sensory patches (neuromasts) distributed in discrete lines over the body surface. The lateral line system is stimulated by local water displacements and vibrations, and detects propulsion of the fish through the water, as well as facilitating shoaling, prey capture, and predator and obstacle avoidance.

events.event: Eye term starts (ZFIN, prim-5); retinal pigmentation begins (Kimmel prim-5, unverified quote).
Choroid fissure rotated to ventral (Schmitt & Dowling 1994 J Comp Neurol 344:532-542 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7929890/).

Lens fiber differentiation 36 to 48 hpf; posterior suture visible (Greiling & Clark 2009 Dev Dyn 238:2254-2265 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19504455/, Dahm et al. 2007 Exp Eye Res 85:74-89 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17467692/).
Focused retinal image; tracking eye movements 73 to 80 hpf; startle to light 68 to 79 hpf (Easter & Nicola 1996 Dev Biol 180:646-663 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8954734/).
Adult eye about 2.5 mm with a 1 mm lens (Bell et al. 2014 Exp Eye Res (adult lens about 1 mm) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4259836/; diameter estimate).

name: retina
definition: Multi-tissue structure that contains the retinal neural layer and the retinal pigmented epithelium, and develops from the optic cup.

spatial.dv: inner lining of the eye cup, medial to the lens
spatial.landmarks: Hemispherical shell facing the lens; optic nerve exits at its ventronasal side through the former choroid fissure.

shape.notes: Thick hemispherical shell (lathe). Outer radius = eye radius minus RPE thickness. Wall thickness (estimates): 60 um at 24 hpf, 90 um at 48 hpf, about 100 um at 5 dpf, 200 to 250 um in the adult.

events.event: Presumptive neural retina (inner cup layer) (ZFA, 26+ somites).
Retina term starts (ZFIN, prim-15).

Continuous growth from the ciliary marginal zone throughout life (Marcus et al. 1999 Vis Neurosci 16:417).

name: retinal pigmented epithelium
definition: A monolayer of pigmented epithelium covering the neural retina; develops from the outer of the two layers of the optic cup.

spatial.dv: outermost layer of the eye cup, between neural retina and sclera
spatial.landmarks: Covers the whole back of the eye; it is the black shell that makes the eye visible from outside from 24 hpf onward.

shape.notes: Thin dark hemispherical shell (5 to 10 um) directly outside the retina. Drive its opacity from 0 at 22 hpf to 1 by about 36 hpf to show pigmentation.

name: lens
definition: Portion of tissue that is a transparent, biconvex structure located in the eye through which light is focused.

spatial.dv: center of the pupil, lateral pole of the eye
spatial.landmarks: Spherical lens filling most of the pupil; it protrudes laterally beyond the eye contour in the larva.

shape.notes: Sphere. Diameter about 63 um at 24 hpf, about 100 um at 5 dpf, 160 um at 15 dpf, 0.75 to 1 mm in adults.

sizes.source: lens volume 0.13e6 um3 at 24 hpf (Kwan et al. 2012 Development 139:359-372 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3243097/); diameter computed for a sphere

lens radius 50.7 um at 5 dpf (Haug et al. 2010 Front Zool 7:8 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2848032/)

events.event: Lens placode (ZFA, 5-9 somites); first visible as a thickening at about 15 hpf (Kwan et al. 2012 Development 139:359-372 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3243097/).
Solid lens vesicle (ZFA, 20-25 somites); round by 20 hpf (Kwan et al. 2012 Development 139:359-372 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3243097/).

Lens pinches off from the ectoderm as a solid cell mass (Kwan et al. 2012 Development 139:359-372 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3243097/, Dahm et al. 2007 Exp Eye Res 85:74-89 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17467692/).
Lens term starts (ZFIN, prim-15).
Posterior suture visible (Greiling & Clark 2009 Dev Dyn 238:2254-2265 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19504455/).
Lens optically functional; image focused on photoreceptors (Easter & Nicola 1996 Dev Biol 180:646-663 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8954734/).

definition: Primordium of the ear epithelium before it hollows into the otic vesicle, present beside the hindbrain rudiment in the mid-segmentation period.

spatial.dv: surface ectoderm lateral to the hindbrain (r5), dorsolateral head
spatial.landmarks: Oval ectodermal thickening beside rhombomere 5, posterior to the eye by about five otic vesicle lengths at 24 hpf (Kimmel OVL).

shape.notes: Flat oval plaque (about 60 x 40 x 15 um) on the lateral head surface. Thicken and hollow it into the otic vesicle at 18 hpf.

sizes.source: estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length)

estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length); placode visible at about 16 hpf (Haddon & Lewis 1996 J Comp Neurol 365:113-128 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8821445/)

Placode visible at 9 to 14 somites (https://zfin.org/zf_info/anatomy/dict/ear/ear.html).
Placode visible at about 16 hpf (Haddon & Lewis 1996 J Comp Neurol 365:113-128 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8821445/).

name: otic vesicle
modelEndNote: ZFIN end stage is Unknown. Hand over to the inner ear term when the semicircular canal pillars have fused (72 hpf).
definition: Epithelial sac present beside the fifth rhombomere; forms the semicircular canals dorsally and the otolith organs ventrally, and houses the acoustico-vestibular sensory epithelia (maculae) of hair cells.

spatial.dv: lateral to the hindbrain at rhombomere 5, dorsal to the pharynx, under the skin
spatial.landmarks: Clear fluid-filled oval behind the eye with two dark otoliths (anterior and posterior). The eye-to-ear gap shrinks from 5 to 0.5 vesicle lengths between 24 and 48 hpf (Kimmel OVL).

shape.notes: Hollow ellipsoid with a thin wall (about 10 um), long axis anteroposterior. From 45 hpf grow three internal pillars (finger-like projections) that fuse by 72 hpf.

sizes.source: estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length); lumen appears at 18 hpf (Haddon & Lewis 1996 J Comp Neurol 365:113-128 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8821445/)
estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length); Kimmel OVL 5 at 24 hpf (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/phar_stgs.html)
estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length); Kimmel OVL 1/2 at 48 hpf (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/hatch_stgs.html)
estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length); ear grows by fluid filling during days 1 to 3 (https://zfin.org/zf_info/anatomy/dict/ear/ear.html)

events.event: Otic vesicle term starts (ZFIN, 14-19 somites).
Lumen forms by cavitation (Haddon & Lewis 1996 J Comp Neurol 365:113-128 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8821445/).
Two otoliths appear (Haddon & Lewis 1996 J Comp Neurol 365:113-128 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8821445/).
First hair cells in two maculae under the otoliths (Haddon & Lewis 1996 J Comp Neurol 365:113-128 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8821445/).
Endolymphatic sac evaginates from the dorsal wall (Swinburne et al. 2018 eLife 7:e37131 https://elifesciences.org/articles/37131).

10 to 20 hair cells per macula (Haddon & Lewis 1996 J Comp Neurol 365:113-128 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8821445/); anterior, lateral and posterior protrusions start 42 to 48 hpf (ZFA, Geng et al. 2013 Development 140:4362-4374 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24067352/).
All three canal pillars fused (Geng et al. 2013 Development 140:4362-4374 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24067352/).

name: inner ear
visibleFromNote: ZFIN start is 20-25 somites (19 hpf), overlapping the otic vesicle. For the model, show the otic vesicle until 72 hpf and the inner ear after that.
definition: The auditory (hearing) and vestibular (balance) organ of the fish, equivalent to the inner ear of amniotes.

spatial.dv: lateral to the hindbrain, inside the otic capsule; utricle dorsal-anterior, saccule ventral-posterior
spatial.landmarks: Behind the eye and lateral to the medulla; in the adult it is enclosed by the prootic, pterotic, sphenotic and exoccipital bones.

shape.notes: Compound: an ellipsoidal vestibule (utricle + saccule) with three semicircular canal tori (anterior, posterior, lateral) on the pars superior. The lagena is a small ventral-posterior pouch from 15 dpf.

sizes.source: estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length); same body as the otic vesicle at this stage (ZFIN inner ear starts at 19 hpf and overlaps the otic vesicle term)
estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length); same body as the otic vesicle at this stage

estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length); adult ear is nearly five times the larval size (Bever & Fekete 2002 Dev Dyn 223:536-543 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11921341/)

events.event: Inner ear term starts (ZFIN, 20-25 somites).
Three semicircular canals formed by 3 dpf (Bever & Fekete 2002 Dev Dyn 223:536-543 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11921341/).
About 80 hair cells per macula between 3 and 7 dpf (Haddon & Lewis 1996 J Comp Neurol 365:113-128 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8821445/).
Lagenar macula with differentiated hair cells by 15 dpf (Bever & Fekete 2002 Dev Dyn 223:536-543 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11921341/).
Adult ear about 2.3 mm long with three otoliths (Bever & Fekete 2002 Dev Dyn 223:536-543 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11921341/, https://zfin.org/zf_info/anatomy/dict/oto/otolith.html).

sources: Haddon & Lewis 1996 J Comp Neurol 365:113-128 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8821445/

name: otolith
definition: Portion of organism substance composed of calcium carbonate located in the otolith organ and positioned over a sensory macula; two form in each vesicle during the late segmentation period.

spatial.dv: inside the otic vesicle lumen; anterior (utricular) otolith dorsal-anterior, posterior (saccular) otolith ventral-posterior
spatial.laterality: paired, two per ear in the embryo, three per ear in the adult
spatial.landmarks: Two dark spheres at the anterior and posterior poles of the otic vesicle. The anterior one becomes the lapillus and the posterior one the sagitta (https://zfin.org/zf_info/anatomy/dict/oto/otolith.html).

shape.notes: Two spheres per ear tethered to the maculae. Adult: three flattened discs (sagitta about 1 mm, lapillus about 0.6 mm, asteriscus about 0.5 mm; estimates).

sizes.source: estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length); visible only with Nomarski optics at 19 hpf (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg_stgs.html)

events.event: Otolith term starts at 18 hpf (https://zfin.org/zf_info/anatomy/dict/oto/otolith.html); ZFIN start 20-25 somites.

Particles coalesce into two otoliths (https://zfin.org/zf_info/anatomy/dict/oto/otolith.html); two otoliths by 19.5 hpf (Haddon & Lewis 1996 J Comp Neurol 365:113-128 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8821445/).

name: semicircular canal
definition: Fluid-filled semicircular tubes, arranged orthogonally to each other in the inner ear. Each canal is associated with a crista that detects angular accelerations.

spatial.dv: dorsal half of the inner ear (pars superior)
spatial.landmarks: Anterior and posterior canals are vertical and meet dorsally in the common crus; the lateral canal is horizontal at the level of the utricle.

shape.notes: Three tori (tube radius about 15 um in the larva, about 100 um in the adult) arranged orthogonally on the dorsal vestibule. Between 45 and 72 hpf, animate three finger-like projections that grow into the vesicle and fuse into pillars. The canals are the spaces left around the pillars.

events.event: Semicircular canal term starts (ZFIN, high-pec).
Epithelial projections push into the vesicle (https://zfin.org/zf_info/anatomy/dict/semi_canal/semi.html, Waterman & Bell 1984 Anat Rec 210:101-114 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/6486477/).

name: olfactory placode
visibleFromNote: ZFIN start is 10-13 somites (14 hpf) for the placodal field. Kimmel first notes the placodes as external thickenings at the 26-somite stage (22 hpf).
definition: Neurogenic placode that gives rise to the olfactory neurons that which convey odor information to the CNS.

spatial.dv: anterior and dorsal to the forebrain, anterolateral head surface, medial to the eyes
spatial.landmarks: Two ectodermal thickenings at the anterior edge of the neural plate, later at the anterior borders of the eyes (Kimmel long-pec).

shape.notes: Flat oval plaque (about 50 x 35 x 20 um) on the snout surface; hollow it into a pit at 30 hpf.

sizes.source: estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length)
estimate (no measured value found; scaled from reference images and body length); placodes thickened at 22 hpf (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg_stgs.html)

events.event: Olfactory field at the anterolateral neural plate edge converges anteriorly (Whitlock & Westerfield 2000 Development 127:3645-3653 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10934010/).
Olfactory placode term starts (ZFIN, 10-13 somites).
Placodes thicken anterior and dorsal to the forebrain (https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/seg_stgs.html).
Axons grow into the forebrain while epidermis still covers the placode (Hansen & Zeiske 1993 J Comp Neurol 333:289-300 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8345108/).
Placode term ends (ZFIN, prim-5); pit opens.

shape.notes: Shallow bowl (lathe) sunk into the snout surface; adult: sac about 1 mm with a rosette of radial lamellae and two nostrils.
